title: Each stalk of an invertible module is a rank-one module
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme, $L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and $y\in Y$. With the stalk module structure of [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], there exists an $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$-linear equivalence $L_y\cong\mathcal O_{Y,y}$.

source.place: Modules Lemma 01CY, proof: the stalk of an invertible module is free of rank one; expanded local trivialization argument (step 3 of lem-weil-pbc-invertible-generating-sections-fibre).

proof.text: Choose an open neighbourhood U of y and an isomorphism of the pullback of L with the unit by IsInvertible.exists_isoUnit. Compose with restrictFunctorIsoPullback, transport the unit free generator across the inverse trivialization, and use isFreeGenerator_restrict_iff to obtain a free generator t of L on U.

The linear map a ↦ a • germ(t) from O_{Y,y} to L_y is bijective. For surjectivity represent a module germ on a neighbourhood V contained in U and write its representing section uniquely as a multiple of t restricted to V. For injectivity represent two scalar germs on neighbourhoods inside U, turn equality of their multiples into section equality on a common smaller neighbourhood using germ_eq, and cancel the restricted free generator. Taking scalar germs then gives equality of the original scalars. LinearMap.toSpanSingleton is this linear map; LinearEquiv.ofBijective and its inverse yield the asserted equivalence. Use the existing stalk_generator_bijective theorem from Sheaf.Paper.NonvanishingSectionTrivializes (accessible via import all); no copy of that theorem is declared here.
